findings.text: Bypass consumer lifecycle exposes register with consumer plus event handle and unregister with consumer alone. Register refuses incomplete callbacks and duplicate handles; unregister is a no-op when no handle is attached and otherwise detaches any linked producer.

Producer and consumer are paired by event-handle identity in separate tables. Linking and unlinking both pause each side first, update mutual linkage callbacks, then resume each side, with pairing pointers cleared on unlink and only set on successful link with rollback on partial failure.

A single global mutex guards bypass table insertion, lookup, removal and the whole link or unlink sequence, so pairing decisions and callback updates appear atomic to concurrent register or unregister callers.

An irqfd is active exactly while linked into the VM active collection. It becomes active during registration, leaves that collection once on deactivate, never returns, and its deferred shutdown work runs after removal.

Testing whether an irqfd is active requires either the irqfd spin lock or SRCU read protection. Removal requires holding that spin lock. Event signaling path must avoid that spin lock, while event closure path may take it because registration holds a reference that excludes overlap.

Signal handling drains the event counter, copies routing under sequence protection and SRCU, then either attempts immediate injection or defers to a worker when inactive or when the architecture reports it must block. Closure handling rechecks activity under lock before deactivating.

Registration refreshes routing before becoming visible to signals, installs an exclusive priority waiter so one event source maps to at most one irqfd across VMs, and only links into the VM collection on waiter success.
Architecture hooks have weak defaults: immediate injection reports that it would block so the caller defers, and bypass stop plus start do nothing unless overridden by the architecture.

Assignment validates interrupt-controller readiness and architecture permission, allocates state, resolves event handles, shares one resampler per signal identity with RCU publication and expedited synchronization, registers under SRCU plus polling, replays a pre-existing pending signal, and registers bypass opportunistically with failure only logged.

Deassignment and VM release deactivate every matching active entry and then wait for all deferred shutdown work, giving the caller a guarantee of no further interrupts on that identity and safe teardown without holding a VM reference.

An ioeventfd record carries a list node, guest address, length, event handle, expected data value, embedded I/O device, bus selector, and a marker selecting wildcard matching versus exact data comparison.

A guest write hits only on exact address equality. Zero length always hits. Otherwise length must match exactly, wildcard always hits, and non-wildcard compares the guest payload at widths one, two, four or eight bytes against the stored value, with other widths missing.
The I/O device write entry signals the event handle on a hit and reports not-supported otherwise. The destructor releases the event reference, unlinks the record and frees it.

Assignment accepts only lengths zero, one, two, four or eight, rejects address plus length wrap, rejects unknown flags, rejects datamatch without length, and selects PIO or virtio-ccw bus from flags with MMIO as default. Collision rejects same bus and address with compatible length and overlapping match criteria.

Ioeventfd assignment and removal serialize on the slot mutex, maintain per-bus device registration and a per-bus counter plus a VM-wide list. Zero-length MMIO is mirrored on a fast bus, with failure during the second insertion rolling back the first.
Top-level irqfd dispatch rejects unknown flags, routes deassign requests to removal and all other valid requests to assignment. Top-level ioeventfd dispatch routes on its deassign flag similarly.
VM event initialization prepares the irqfd spin lock, active list, resampler list and resampler mutex where interrupt-chip support exists, plus the VM-wide ioeventfd list.

Resampler creation and sharing serialize on a dedicated resampler mutex. Ioeventfd list and bus membership serialize on the slot mutex. Irqfd active membership and routing serialize on the irqfd spin lock taken with interrupt protection, with a sequence counter tied to that lock.

Guest memory file state pairs a per-open record holding owning VM, binding table and list node with a per-inode record holding sharing policy, VFS inode, file list and flags. A file-system mount pointer is kept privately, and iteration walks the inode file list.

Shared versus private is complementary for a given file offset. Invalidate filtering selects shared when the file was created init-shared and private otherwise. Invalidate start walks bindings overlapping the requested file interval, maps each overlap into guest frame numbers, holds MMU protection once while unmapping each affected range, and flushes remote TLBs once if any unmap requested it.
MMU unmap for a guest frame interval first records the interval for invalidation tracking and then performs the unmap, returning whether a TLB flush is needed.

Observed control flags include irqfd deassign and resample, and ioeventfd deassign, datamatch, PIO and virtio-ccw-notify with MMIO as default bus; ioeventfd lengths are limited to zero, one, two, four and eight. Numeric values are not shown in these fragments.

Closure racing with KVM-side deactivation must retest activity after acquiring locks because deactivation precedes wait-queue removal. Poll registration briefly hides lock ownership from deadlock detection around exclusive waiter insertion because signaling and registration use opposite locking rules.
